subject: general
question: Which of the following colonial-era buildings in Chennai serves as the headquarters of the Greater Chennai Corporation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ripon Building**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ripon Building** is the headquarters of the **Greater Chennai Corporation**, the civic body that governs the city of Chennai, Tamil Nadu.
 
• It was constructed in the year **1913** during the British colonial rule in India and is named after **Lord Ripon**, who served as the **Viceroy of India** from 1880 to 1884.
 
• The building is a fine example of **Neo-Classical architecture**, with influences from the Gothic, Ionic, and Corinthian styles.
 
• The Ripon Building is a white structure made of **chunam (lime plaster)** and is notable for its **200-foot-long frontage**, a central tower, and a clock known as the Westminster Chimes.
 
• The building is situated near **Park Town**, opposite the Chennai Central railway station, making it a prominent landmark of the city.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Court**:

 
 
• The **Madras High Court**, established in **1862**, is one of the three High Courts in India created under Queen Victoria's charter.
 
• It is located on **NSC Bose Road** in Chennai and is known for its **Indo-Saracenic architecture**.
 
• The High Court is the principal judicial body of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry and does not serve as the headquarters of the Greater Chennai Corporation.
 
 
 
• **Fort St. George**:
 
 
• **Fort St. George** was built in **1644** by the British East India Company and is considered the first English fortress in India.
 
• It is located on the eastern coast of Chennai and currently houses the administrative offices of the Tamil Nadu Government and the Legislative Assembly.
 
• Though historically significant, it is not the headquarters of the Greater Chennai Corporation.
 
 
 
• **Government Museum**:
 
 
• The **Government Museum**, also known as the Egmore Museum, is located in Chennai and was established in **1851**.
 
• It is the **second oldest museum in India** and houses a rich collection of artifacts, including bronze sculptures, archaeological findings, and rare coins.
 
• The museum is dedicated to preserving historical and cultural artifacts and does not serve as the headquarters of the Greater Chennai Corporation.
 
 
 
• **Ripon Building**:
 
 
• The Ripon Building is named after **Lord Ripon**, who is often referred to as the "Father of Local Self-Government in India."
 
• The building is an iconic structure in Chennai and represents the city’s colonial past.
 
• The **clock tower**, which is 43 meters high, houses a clock known as the **Westminster Chimes**, which was installed in 1913 and continues to function till date.
 
• The Ripon Building is used for administrative purposes and is the central office for city governance in Chennai.
